clue.text: King Charles holding miss tighter

indicators.note: the king's title is pictured gripping another word between its two letters

blocks.note: Carolus Rex, the Latin royal cipher of King Charles
to miss something is to lose it

explanation.surface: A monarch keeps a firmer grip on a young lady.
explanation.walkthrough: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles; it splits round LOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Closer is the comparative of close, meaning more firmly fastened or packed.

clue.text: Stroke a crocodile?

blocks.note: first meaning: a drawn mark of the pen
second meaning: a crocodile is a file of schoolchildren walking in pairs

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites patting a reptile; in Britain a crocodile is also a column of schoolchildren walking two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen stroke drawn across paper is a mark of this kind, and a queue of pupils forms one too.

clue.text: Fleck on pattern of squares not covering everyone

blocks.note: a fleck is a small spot
check is a chequered pattern

explanation.surface: A speck on a tartan or gingham fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a test made on a sample only.
explanation.definitionFit: A random inspection examines only a sample of people or items rather than every single one.

clue.text: Fellow sun-god has short climb

indicators.note: a short version of the word lacks its final letter

blocks.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun-god
to scale is to climb

explanation.surface: A man worshipping the sun takes a brief clamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellow is an informal word for a man or chap, and a rascal is a roguish chap.

clue.text: Florence dominated by struggle

blocks.note: Flo is the pet form of the name Florence
someone dominated is under another's control

explanation.surface: A woman named Florence is overpowered in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence looks like the Italian city but it is the woman's name, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to struggle clumsily, thrashing about as in mud or water.

clue.text: Winding up poker players, perhaps, in girls' establishment

blocks.note: winding up a task is finishing it
a school is a group of gamblers playing together

explanation.surface: Closing down a card game run in a girls' boarding house.
explanation.walkthrough: A school, besides a place of learning, is a regular group of card players.
explanation.definitionFit: A private college where young women were taught social graces and etiquette before entering society.

clue.text: Being old, died single at half-term

definitions.note: a phrase for the state rather than a plain adjective

indicators.note: only half of the following word is kept, its first two letters

blocks.note: ob. is the abbreviation of Latin obiit, he or she died
sole means single, the only one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly person passed away alone during the school break.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, from Latin obiit, is found on gravestones and in reference books.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolete is outdated and no longer in use, past its time.

clue.text: Company longs to show what is in hosiery

indicators.note: the letters are on show inside the run of the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A firm is eager to display its stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings and tights are typically made from this synthetic fibre, so it is what hosiery contains.

clue.text: Shut up about our being fostered!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word is placed round the second

blocks.note: shut up in a cage
taken as written

explanation.surface: An indignant protest at being locked up because of being foster children.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster growth or hope is to promote and support it, which is what encouraging does.

clue.text: Set free none with soul in torment

indicators.note: letters in torment are twisted and wrenched out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Release nobody whose spirit suffers torture.
explanation.definitionFit: To unloosen is to loosen or untie, letting something go free from its bonds.

clue.text: RAF man sitting inside only console

indicators.note: one piece is seated within the other word

blocks.note: sole means only
AC is aircraftman, the lowest rank in the RAF

explanation.surface: An airman alone in a cockpit, with only the instrument console for company.
explanation.walkthrough: Console looks like a control panel noun but it is the verb to comfort; AC is aircraftman, a junior RAF rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To console someone is to give them comfort, and solace is that comfort as a noun, also used as a verb.

clue.text: For reclining, his canoe is fixed with glue

definitions.note: describes the purpose of the thing rather than naming it

indicators.note: fixed here means rigged or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man mends his canoe with adhesive so he can lie back in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long upholstered sofa-like seat with a backrest at one end, designed for lounging with the legs stretched out.

clue.text: Congratulate this cat: I feel it moving

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise this cat: an owner is touched by the animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram feels apt, as the word sounds feline.
explanation.definitionFit: To felicitate is a formal way of offering someone congratulations on good fortune.

clue.text: Mother of Paris seen in lake

blocks.note: first meaning: the French word for mother
second meaning: a poetic or dialect word for a lake or pond

explanation.surface: Paris's mother, perhaps a goddess, appears at a lakeside.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris may suggest the Trojan prince, but it signals French.
explanation.definitionFit: Mère is French for mother, and a mere is an English word for a small lake.

clue.text: It's essential to break tin with broad back

indicators.note: to break the word is to smash its letters into a new order
back tells us to read the adjective from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
broad means large

explanation.surface: Instructions for opening a can using a wide back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something integral is a necessary part of the whole, indispensable to it.

clue.text: Ecological space for those off stage

definitions.note: describes the room's use rather than naming it

blocks.note: green means environmentally friendly
room means space

explanation.surface: An environmentally friendly area set aside for backstage performers.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre, actors wait and relax in this lounge when they are not performing.

clue.text: Baby-sitter bills holding up the books

indicators.note: the words hold the answer within their letters
in a down clue, up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the run of letters straddles the gap between the second and third words

explanation.surface: A childminder's invoices delay the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: The books sounds like accounts, but it means the texts of operas.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the written text of an opera, so libretti are those books of words.

clue.text: Summoning by bell, tense with suspicion

blocks.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
an inkling is a vague suspicion

explanation.surface: Ringing for a servant, nervous and wary.
explanation.walkthrough: Tense looks like an adjective about nerves, but it is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinkle a small bell is to ring it lightly, as when calling a servant.

clue.text: Uniform is unruffled

blocks.note: first meaning: the same throughout, regular
second meaning: calm and level, as of temper

explanation.surface: A smart outfit stays neat and uncrumpled.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something level and consistent: a regular rate, and a calm temperament.

clue.text: Type of skirt, but where is the point of it?

definitions.text: where is the point of it?

blocks.note: first meaning: a slim, straight, close-fitting skirt

blocks.clueFragment: where is the point of it?
blocks.note: second meaning: a writing tool that is sharpened to a point

explanation.walkthrough: The second half sounds like a grumble that the skirt is pointless; literally it asks for a thing that has a sharp tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow tailored skirt shares its name with the graphite writing stick, which famously has a point.

clue.text: Side of beef with cover for stargazers?

definitions.note: describes the screen's use rather than naming it

blocks.note: silverside is a cut of beef, so this word sits beside side in it
a screen is a cover or shield

explanation.surface: A butcher's joint with a protective wrapping, offered to astronomers.
explanation.walkthrough: Silverside is a British cut of beef from the hindquarter. The stars here are film stars, not astronomers' ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase stands for the cinema, where audiences gaze at the film stars on the big picture.

clue.text: At six, boy rises to get some plonk

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad gets up at six o'clock to fetch cheap wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Plonk is British slang for cheap wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vino is a jokey word for wine, especially cheap wine, so vinos are some plonk.

clue.text: In this place he must join the Royal Engineers

blocks.note: taken as written
RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: An army recruitment slogan: he must enlist with the sappers here.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb indicates the present location, the spot where the speaker currently is.

clue.text: Is attractive when married with silver bag

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining a noun: the thing that attracts

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
to net is to bag or catch

explanation.surface: A bride is appealing on her wedding day, carrying a silver handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet is an object that pulls iron towards it, the thing that draws things in.

clue.text: Quick inspection long ago finished

blocks.note: once means at some time in the past
over means finished

explanation.surface: A brief look-over, completed ages ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving something the once-over means examining it rapidly and superficially.

clue.text: Paper carrier?

blocks.note: surface reading: a bag or envelope that holds sheets
setter's reading: a young person who delivers newspapers on a round

explanation.walkthrough: Paper carrier suggests a carrier bag made of paper; the paper is a daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A young female who delivers daily newspapers to homes on a morning round.

clue.text: Allowed to imprison demon and hanger-on

indicators.note: imprisoning one word means locking it within another

blocks.note: let means allowed
an imp is a little demon

explanation.surface: Permission is granted to lock up a devil and its follower.
explanation.walkthrough: Hanger-on looks like a person; it is the shellfish that clings to rocks, also a figurative clinger.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet clings tightly to rocks, so the name is used for a person who sticks to another.
